newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets support curbs on German pig exports.
newsitem.headline: EU vets support curbs on German pig exports.

text.p: The European Union's standing veterinary committee supported a partial ban on the export of pigs from Germany because of swine fever, the Commission said in a statement on Thursday.
The ban, based on a Commission proposal, will be formally adopted in the next day or two, the statement added.
The export of pigs to another EU member state from five Laender (states) and two districts in a sixth will be stopped.
Movement of pigs to other parts of Germany is banned and infected pigs must be slaughtered in the infected zone or in a specified abattoir.

Export of pigs from a closed Laender to another member state will be possible provided the animals come from uninfected areas and are kept in a closed holding for 30 days under veterinary supervision.
The ban may be lifted after 60 days if there is no new outbreak of swine fever.
